findings.question: How common are financial inclusion and mobile-money adoption?
findings.finding: The weighted financial-inclusion estimate is 43.1%; the weighted mobile-money estimate is 50.4%.
findings.interpretation: Mobile-money adoption is more common than financial-institution account ownership in the weighted descriptive estimates.

findings.question: Does financial access differ by education?
findings.finding: Financial inclusion is 82.4% among respondents with tertiary education or more and 36.8% among those with primary education or less.
findings.interpretation: Education level is associated with a large descriptive financial-inclusion gap.

findings.question: Does financial access differ by household income?
findings.finding: Financial inclusion rises from 34.1% in quintile 1 to 65.0% in quintile 5.
findings.interpretation: Higher income quintiles are associated with higher financial-inclusion rates, although mobile-money rates are not perfectly monotonic across all quintiles.

findings.question: Does workforce participation matter descriptively?
findings.finding: Financial inclusion is 55.8% in the workforce and 30.6% outside it.
findings.interpretation: Workforce participation is associated with higher observed financial inclusion and mobile-money adoption.

findings.question: How is recent internet use associated with the outcomes?
findings.finding: Mobile-money adoption is 60.5% among recent internet users and 39.7% in the combined zero category.
findings.interpretation: Recent internet use is associated with higher observed financial inclusion and mobile-money adoption.

findings.question: How is mobile-phone ownership associated with mobile money?
findings.finding: Mobile-money adoption is 55.2% among phone owners and 20.4% among respondents reporting no phone.
findings.interpretation: Phone ownership is associated with a sizeable mobile-money adoption gap.
